title: Identification of Local Average Direct and Spillover Effects in Stepped-Wedge Rollouts with Interference
banked_reason: Mathematically sound sharp support results, but the cold referee capped the package at subfield (6.7 < 7.4) because the promised implemented formula-or-twins compiler was not delivered and no bounded same-topic repair could reach field.
gap_reasons: The formula-or-twins result establishes only a terminating exhaustive procedure; it provides no implementation, complexity control, or reproducible certificate artifacts, so the framing of it as an engine overstates its practical delivery.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived source-faithful sharp observable-support criteria and rational twins for LADE, arbitrary-recipient LAIE, and LASE, including exact fixed-count and graph-degree consequences; the mathematics referee passed the package. The field-tier framing collapsed because the advertised paired-LP certificate compiler was only an abstract terminating enumeration, not an implementation with reproducible artifacts or complexity control. A follow-on should reuse the theorem package but either deliver that constructive layer plus a field-level methodological consequence or honestly frame the result at subfield scope.
tldr: When do the exact Hoshino--Yanagi local-average direct, indirect, and spillover targets survive the dependent support of a stepped-wedge rollout? The note proves sharp, target-specific observable-fiber characterizations and gives explicit identifying functionals or rational same-law twins. In a balanced fixed-count rollout, arbitrary-recipient \(\mathrm{LAIE}_S\) is identified exactly when every focal recipient set is empty, in which case it is zero; otherwise perfect-compliance twins establish nonidentification without connectedness or disjointness assumptions. Neighbor-count LASE support reduces to exact degree-based path, star, and complete-graph design rules.
gap: The anchor theory assumes mutually independent instruments for LADE and LAIE and proves only a sufficient Appendix-E ratio for LASE. Balanced stepped wedges instead impose dependent fixed-count assignments, and the current stepped-wedge noncompliance literature rules out the cross-cluster interference central to these targets. No inspected paper provides exact finite-support necessity, a LAIE denominator twin, or the stated graph/design frontier.
fill: Prove three support iff theorems under the source-faithful target assumptions, give observable functionals and rational nonidentification twins, solve balanced fixed-count neighbor-count LASE combinatorially, and implement a receipt-stratified exact certificate engine for restricted supports and edge cases.
